selected_grant.title: Clean Water State Revolving Fund
selected_grant.agency: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy
eligible_applicants: City or township governmentsCounty governmentsSpecial district governments
selected_grant.overview: The Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF) provides low-interest loans to counties, cities, villages, townships, authorities, and other public entities for projects that improve water quality and protect public health. It finances statewide wastewater and stormwater infrastructure as well as nonpoint source (NPS) pollution control needs.Applicants must be public entities created under state law. Disadvantaged communities (Overburdened or Significantly Overburdened) receive priority points and principal forgiveness.Eligible projects include wastewater treatment works, stormwater management, and nonpoint source pollution control. Projects must comply with Davis-Bacon, American Iron and Steel, and Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements.The application process involves submitting an Intent to Apply (ITA) form by November 1st, followed by an Overburdened Determination Survey and final project planning documents by May 1st. Projects are scored and ranked on a Project Priority List (PPL). Show More

packet_draft.project_title: Unnamed Township Water Flood Mitigation Planning Project
packet_draft.problem_statement: Repeated heavy rain events cause flooding along a residential road corridor near a school bus route and senior households. The flooding overwhelms roadside ditches and undersized culverts, resulting in road closures, basement seepage, and unsafe shoulder conditions. Planning is needed to develop drainage engineering, culvert replacement, ditch restoration, and stormwater design solutions.
packet_draft.public_benefit: Addressing the flooding would improve road safety for residents, including seniors and schoolchildren, and reduce disruptions to daily travel. Improved drainage infrastructure can enhance community resilience to future storm events. The project supports water quality and public health goals outlined by the grant program.
packet_draft.funding_request_summary: The township seeks a cost estimate of $850000 to support engineering design, culvert replacement, and stormwater improvements. The Clean Water State Revolving Fund is identified as a potential funding source that may support part of the project. A detailed budget and cost‑share plan should be developed before submission.
packet_draft.council_memo: Staff have prepared a preliminary plan to address flooding on a residential road corridor affecting seniors and school transportation. The Clean Water State Revolving Fund appears to be a potential funding source, but grant status, deadline, and match requirements are still unverified. Several required documents, including an Intent to Apply form and a council resolution, are missing. It is recommended that the council approve further preparation work to close these gaps before any application is submitted.
resident_faq: What is the purpose of this project? The township plans to improve drainage and replace undersized culverts to reduce flooding along a residential road that affects seniors and school bus routes.
Why is this project important for residents? Reducing flooding will improve road safety, prevent basement water intrusion, and enhance community resilience to heavy rain events.

How could the Clean Water State Revolving Fund help? The grant may provide low‑interest loan funding for stormwater infrastructure, but eligibility, match requirements, and exact funding limits need confirmation.

What steps remain before funding can be secured? Staff need to verify the grant’s open status, confirm application deadlines, obtain required forms, develop a council resolution, and finalize engineering design and cost estimates.

Confirm the exact application deadline dates and year for the Intent to Apply and final submission
Determine whether a match or cost‑share is required and assess availability of match funds
Obtain the Intent to Apply form, Overburdened Determination Survey, and final project planning documents
Gather missing applicant profile information such as community name, county, and population
Develop a council resolution authorizing the project and the engineering design memo
Create a detailed cost estimate and budget documentation for the $850000 project

selected_grant.overview: The Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF) provides low-interest loans to counties, cities, villages, townships, authorities, and other public entities for projects that improve water quality and protect public health. It finances statewide wastewater and stormwater infrastructure as well as nonpoint source (NPS) pollution control needs.Applicants must be public entities created under state law. Disadvantaged communities (Overburdened or Significantly Overburdened) receive priority points and principal forgiveness.Eligible projects include wastewater treatment works, stormwater management, and nonpoint source pollution control. Projects must comply with Davis-Bacon, American Iron and Steel, and Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements.The application process involves submitting an Intent to Apply (ITA) form by November 1st, followed by an Overburdened Determination Survey and final project planning documents by May 1st. Projects are scored and ranked on a Project Priority List (PPL). Show More
